primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: PKP2 encodes plakophilin-2, a desmosomal component of cardiomyocyte intercalated-disc junctions. Pathogenic PKP2 variants impair desmosomal integrity and mechanical coupling, contributing to ventricular arrhythmias and progressive fibrofatty myocardial replacement.
vignette: A 25-year-old competitive cyclist has exertional palpitations and syncope. His older brother died suddenly at age 29. Cardiac MRI shows regional right-ventricular akinesia with fibrofatty myocardial replacement. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic loss-of-function variant in PKP2.
lead: The affected protein normally contributes most directly to which of the following cellular structures?
correct: Desmosomal junctions that mechanically couple adjacent cardiomyocytes at intercalated discs
distractors: Gap junction channels that permit direct ionic current between adjacent cardiomyocytes
Costameres that link the sarcomeric cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix
Sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium-release channels that initiate excitation-contraction coupling
Tight junctions that seal the paracellular space between epithelial cells
distractor_notes: Gap junctions provide electrical coupling primarily through connexins; PKP2 is a desmosomal junction protein.
Costameres connect myofibrils to the extracellular matrix through proteins such as dystrophin and integrins, not plakophilin-2.
Cardiac ryanodine receptors mediate sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium release; PKP2 is not a calcium-release channel.
Tight junctions form epithelial permeability barriers and are not the specialized mechanical junction affected by PKP2-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
key_expl: Plakophilin-2 is a major cardiac desmosomal protein at intercalated discs. Desmosomes mechanically couple adjacent cardiomyocytes and anchor cytoskeletal intermediate filaments. PKP2 deficiency disrupts junctional integrity and is a major genetic cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, which is characterized by ventricular arrhythmias and fibrofatty myocardial replacement.
objective: Identify PKP2/plakophilin-2 as a cardiac desmosomal junction protein implicated in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
